policy: P0-D: register SHA-256 + backup path for critical weights/data; lost-but-reproducible artifacts carry reproduce command
identity_policy: 2026-08-31: torch.save is byte-non-deterministic across runs of the same state_dict (64-byte storage alignment padding over zip entries). For .pth files, sha256 is a snapshot of one serialization, NOT an identity - match on content_digest (sorted key|shape|dtype + per-tensor payload hash) plus a size tolerance. safetensors/.onnx are deterministic, so sha256 stays authoritative there.

artifacts.name: matting_prod_fp16
artifacts.note: 2026-08-31 re-derived, not recovered from cloud: the 08-30 gitlink de-index destroyed the original external/birefnet/ copy and no fp16 existed remotely. Registered sha/size belong to the lost serialization; content_digest is unchanged in substance because it derives from the byte-identical mixed checkpoint. Two derivations in the same run differed by 12616 bytes - see identity_policy. KNOWN NUMERIC DEFECT (pre-existing, inherited from mixed, not introduced here): decoder.decoder_block4.bn_in.running_var fp32 max 201115.34 > fp16 max 65504, so it becomes inf and that BatchNorm emits a constant bias at eval. Cannot be fixed inside the checkpoint (a runtime doing model.half() then load_state_dict re-casts the fp32 running_var to inf; clamping to 65504 is a different wrong value). Remedy is runtime-side: use autocast (BatchNorm is on the fp32 autocast whitelist) or exclude BN layers from .half(). Also 43 num_batches_tracked int buffers overflow to fp16 inf (training-only, unused at eval) and 24 relative_position_index buffers (max 528) stay exactly representable.

artifacts.name: camera_lora_v3b_prod
artifacts.val_acc_caveat: 0.4603 is inflated, not a clean measurement. The split is index-level with no shot/clip grouping (train_anime_camera_v5.py:745-748) while time_reverse defaults ON and appends a mirrored twin of the SAME clip (134-139); because SIX_MAP and REVERSE_PAIR are both keyed by the fine movement_label, twins fire even for six-schema runs. Measured straddle on local vlm_labels.jsonl (33764 expanded samples, n_val 5064): 4032 of 15814 twin pairs land on opposite sides = 0.2550 vs theory 2*0.15*0.85 = 0.2550. Same-clip presence on both sides inflates accuracy; valid comparison requires shot-level splits plus class-balanced accuracy against the 0.4387 majority-class floor.

artifacts.note: 2026-08-31 confirmed HARD LOSS. Absent in repo, absent on AutoDL (remote _fixed dir holds only adapter_config.json / adapter_model.safetensors / meta.json), and no git blob exists because .gitignore:109 'output/' also matches models/output/. Deliberately NOT restored: a different 300-byte coarse-key thresholds_tuned.json (sha256 b3d6383c...) exists in the tree and is a different artifact with different keys - substituting it would be silently wrong. Functional consequence of the absence, superseded 2026-09-01: the code no longer invents fallback thresholds. models/anime_camera_classifier.py _load_thresholds(path, labels) returns None and logs a warning whenever the sidecar is missing, unparsable, or fails to cover every label, and _predict then uses plain argmax. Previously the absence failed open: the coarse-key fallback intersected nothing with the fine schema, so all ten labels silently shared a hardcoded 0.4 while looking calibrated. Predictions are unchanged, because a uniform threshold is a no-op for top-1 selection; what changed is that the degradation is loud instead of invisible.
